speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have jaundice, itching, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine; this pattern suggests an obstruction of the bile ducts. To narrow this down, have you recently experienced any pain in the right upper quadrant of your abdomen, particularly after eating fatty foods?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. The patient has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 year...

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of alcohol use is significant, but your current symptoms of weight loss and pale stools strongly suggest a mass obstructing the common bile duct rather than simple stones. Did you notice any specific pain in the upper right abdomen, especially after eating fatty meals? Also, have you had any fever or chills recently?

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; your age, smoking background, and the combination of painless jaundice with significant weight loss are highly concerning for pancreatic malignancy. Have you noticed any new lumps or swelling in your abdomen, and have you experienced any recent changes in bowel movements other than the pale color? REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen with Contrast; REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan showing normal readings is very surprising given your severe weight loss and jaundice; could you describe the nature of that pain from three years ago, and do you have any history of gallstones or previous abdominal surgeries? REQUEST TEST: MRI Abdomen with MRCP; REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Abdomen with MRCP: The examination reveals a 3.2 cm hypovascular mass in the head of the pancreas causing obstruction of the main pancreatic duct and the common bile duct. There is associated dilation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts (double duct sign). A small amount of ascites is present. No distant metastases are visualized in the liver or lungs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma of the Head of the Pancreas. The imaging findings of a hypovascular mass in the pancreatic head causing the "double duct sign" and obstructive jaundice are classic for this malignancy. Would you like to discuss treatment options or further staging?
